title: Why We Made Path Pal
text:
It started with a simple observation: while some students had access to private college counselors, expensive test prep, and personalized guidance, many public school students were navigating the college application process completely alone.

We saw students who had the potential to get into great schools but didn't know where to start. They didn't know which colleges matched their profile, how to improve their chances, or what activities would strengthen their applications. Their schools were understaffed, with one counselor responsible for hundreds of students. Private counseling cost thousands of dollars that their families couldn't afford.

That's when we realized something had to change. Every student deserves access to quality college guidance, regardless of their school's resources or their family's income. So we built Path Pal.

Path Pal was created to level the playing field. We wanted to give every student, especially those in public schools without dedicated college counselors, the same tools and guidance that were previously only available to those who could pay for it.

Our AI counselor is available 24/7, answering questions about college admissions, course selection, and test preparation. Our admissions odds calculator shows students where they stand and how to improve. Our "What If" simulator lets them test different scenarios before making changes. All of this is free and accessible to anyone.

We built Path Pal because we believe that access to quality college guidance shouldn't depend on your zip code or your family's income. Every student deserves a fair shot at reaching their dream schools, and we're here to make sure they get it.

This is more than just an app to us. It's our mission to ensure that every student, regardless of their circumstances, has the tools and support they need to succeed. That's why we made Path Pal.

title: College Admissions in 2026: What's Changed?
text:
College admissions has shifted in meaningful ways over the past few years, and for students applying in 2026, three areas matter more than ever: testing, extracurriculars, and essays. Understanding how these have changed can help you make smarter decisions and avoid wasting time on things that no longer move the needle.

Many colleges are now test-optional, meaning SAT or ACT scores are no longer required. But that doesn't mean they're irrelevant. In 2026, test scores are best thought of as optional tools, not automatic requirements. Strong scores can still strengthen an application, especially at more selective schools or for competitive majors. On the other hand, submitting weak scores can hurt more than help. Admissions officers now evaluate test scores in context—alongside your high school, course rigor, and available opportunities. The key change is that students have more choice. The challenge is knowing when that choice benefits you.

The days of joining clubs just to pad a résumé are fading. Admissions officers now focus far more on depth, commitment, and impact than on long activity lists. In 2026, colleges care about how long you stuck with something, whether you took initiative or leadership, and what you actually contributed or built. One meaningful project, job, or long-term commitment can outweigh multiple surface-level activities. Colleges want to understand how you spend your time, and what that says about your interests, values, and curiosity.

As applications become more holistic, essays have become one of the most important ways to stand out. Strong essays in 2026 don't just list accomplishments. They show how you think, reflect on why experiences mattered, and connect past actions to future goals. Generic essays are easy to spot and easy to forget. Admissions officers want to understand who you are beyond grades and activities, and essays are often the clearest window into that.

College admissions in 2026 rewards intentional choices over box-checking. Students who understand how tests, activities, and essays really work can focus their energy where it matters most and approach the process with far more confidence.

title: Your Dream School is Closer Than You Think
text:
For many students, a "dream school" feels exactly like that: a dream. Something impressive, distant, and reserved for other people with perfect grades, massive acctivities, or inside knowledge. But the truth is, getting into a top college is far less about being perfect and far more about being intentional. Most successful applicants don't stumble into their dream schools. They plan their way there.

One of the biggest misconceptions about elite colleges is that they're only looking for one type of student. In reality, top schools are building communities, not rankings spreadsheets. They want students with clear interests, genuine curiosity, and evidence that they've used their time well. That means you don't need to do everything, you need to do the right things for you. What sets strong applicants apart is not the number of activities they list, but the story those activities tell. Admissions officers look for direction. Did you explore an interest over time? Did you take initiative? Did you grow, lead, or build something meaningful? A focused, authentic application almost always stands out more than a crowded but shallow one.

Another reason dream schools feel out of reach is timing. Many students wait until junior year to think seriously about college, which turns the process into a stressful scramble. But when you start earlier—even just by understanding what colleges value—you give yourself room to make smarter choices. You can pick classes intentionally, commit to activities you care about, and build experiences that actually matter. Essays also play a huge role in closing the gap between "dream" and "possible." Strong essays don't try to impress with achievements alone. They explain why experiences mattered, how you think, and what motivates you. They help admissions officers see you as a real person, not just an application.

The biggest shift to make is mental. Instead of asking, "Am I good enough for this school?" the better question is, "How can I build the strongest version of my story over time?" When you focus on growth, clarity, and intention, dream schools stop feeling mythical and start feeling reachable.

Your dream school isn't closer because standards are lower. It's closer because the path is clearer than most students realize. With the right plan, what once felt impossible can become realistic—and even likely.
